summary: Generalize the existing ClawMobile inbound pre-model fast path into Capability-First dispatch backed by the canonical Capability Graph.
reason: Known capabilities could reach a provider before Claw routing, allowing provider-generated refusals and unnecessary model calls. Local Companion turns could also lose senderIsOwner and skip the pre-model path.

tests.name: gemini-request
tests.evidence: 20 Python tests passed; Known hit/error bypass provider while miss/assist retain model path.

tests.name: capability-first-plugin
tests.evidence: Local Companion owner fallback, remote isolation, hit/known_error handling and assist/miss fallthrough passed.

tests.name: mcp-bridge
tests.evidence: Existing external MCP shadow/write/status/artifact/context suite passed.

tests.name: remote-bridge-core
tests.evidence: Existing idempotence, task/step receipt, process, artifact and Continuum effect-fence suite passed.

capabilities.reason: Capability truth and execution contracts remain in ui-playbooks; this runtime consumes the canonical Graph before model invocation.

architecture.reason: Extends the existing inbound_claim/model-fast-path hook and existing Capability Graph. The architecture decision is owned by ui-playbooks ADR-20261008-capability-first; no new component or source of truth is introduced.

rollback: Revert this scoped runtime commit, rebuild/install the existing mobile-ui plugin and restart Companion through the supervised path.
limitations: Only declared inert pre_model_handoff contracts can cross a confirmation-required pre-model path.
Remote channels do not inherit the local Companion owner fallback.
Live transactional acceptance remains a separate human-boundary test; this delivery does not remove biometric or issuer controls.
